tools.name: street_cleaning_schedule
tools.description: Look up the upcoming City of Chicago street cleaning dates for a street address, plus its ward and section. Use when someone asks when street cleaning / street sweeping is on their block, or whether they need to move their car. Chicago only. Source: the City's published street cleaning schedule.

tools.name: permit_zone_lookup
tools.description: Check whether a Chicago street address is in a residential permit parking zone, which zone, and the hours a permit is required. Use when someone asks if they can park on a block without a permit, or what zone their address is in. Chicago only. Source: City permit zone records and ordinance hours.

tools.name: ticket_win_rate
tools.description: How often Chicago parking and camera tickets of a given type are dismissed when contested by mail, from the City's own hearing records (obtained under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act). Omit violation_type for the overall rate and the list of types.

tools.name: should_i_contest
tools.description: Plain-language guidance for someone holding a Chicago parking or camera ticket: the deadline, how often that ticket type is dismissed, the reason that most often wins, and where to get help contesting it. Not legal advice.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "sign_up_for_autopilot" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: sign_up_for_autopilot, ticket_win_rate, should_i_contest · Private data: permit_zone_lookup, ticket_win_rate · Public sink: free_street_cleaning_alerts, sign_up_for_autopilot.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: sign_up_for_autopilot, ticket_win_rate, should_i_contest · Private data: permit_zone_lookup, ticket_win_rate · Public sink: free_street_cleaning_alerts, sign_up_for_autopilot

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
